title: Peripheral Nervous System, ANS, and Reflexes

cranial_nerves.mnemonic_names: Oh Oh Oh To Touch And Feel Very Good Velvet, AH! — Olfactory, Optic, Oculomotor, Trochlear, Trigeminal, Abducens, Facial, Vestibulocochlear, Glossopharyngeal, Vagus, Accessory, Hypoglossal
cranial_nerves.mnemonic_type: Some Say Marry Money But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More — S=Sensory, M=Motor, B=Both

I_olfactory.function: SMELL. from nasal mucosa → olfactory bulb. only CN that goes to cortex WITHOUT passing through thalamus.

II_optic.function: VISION. from retina → thalamus (LGN) → visual cortex. tested with eye chart, visual fields.

III_oculomotor.function: moves eye (4 of 6 extrinsic eye muscles: superior/inferior/medial rectus + inferior oblique). raises eyelid (levator palpebrae). parasympathetic: constricts pupil + accommodates lens. damage → ptosis (drooping eyelid), eye turns out+down, dilated pupil.

IV_trochlear.function: SUPERIOR OBLIQUE muscle only. turns eye inferolaterally (down and out). SMALLEST CN. only CN that exits from POSTERIOR brainstem. damage → diplopia (double vision) looking down.

branches.V2_maxillary: sensory. cheek, upper lip, upper teeth, palate.
branches.V3_mandibular: both. sensory: lower face, lower teeth, tongue (touch, not taste). motor: MUSCLES OF MASTICATION (masseter, temporalis, pterygoids).

V_trigeminal.note: LARGEST CN. main sensory nerve of face. trigeminal neuralgia = excruciating facial pain.

VI_abducens.function: LATERAL RECTUS muscle only. ABducts eye (turns outward). damage → eye can't look laterally → medial deviation.

VII_facial.motor: muscles of FACIAL EXPRESSION (frontalis, orbicularis oculi, orbicularis oris, buccinator, platysma, etc). also stapedius (dampens sound).
VII_facial.parasympathetic: submandibular + sublingual salivary glands. lacrimal glands (tears).
VII_facial.damage: Bell's palsy — unilateral facial paralysis. can't close eye, corner of mouth droops, can't wrinkle forehead on affected side.

VIII_vestibulocochlear.function: two branches: VESTIBULAR (balance, equilibrium from semicircular canals + otolith organs) + COCHLEAR (hearing from cochlea). damage → deafness, vertigo, nystagmus.

IX_glossopharyngeal.sensory: taste from posterior 1/3 of tongue. sensory from pharynx. monitors blood pressure (carotid sinus baroreceptors) + blood O2/CO2 (carotid body chemoreceptors).

X_vagus.what: WANDERER. longest CN. extends into thorax + abdomen.
X_vagus.parasympathetic: HEART (slows HR), LUNGS (constricts bronchioles), GI tract (increases motility + secretion) — basically runs the 'rest and digest' for thorax + abdomen.
X_vagus.sensory: visceral sensation from thorax + abdomen. tiny bit of taste (epiglottis).
X_vagus.damage: hoarseness (recurrent laryngeal nerve). if both sides damaged → can't swallow or speak.

XI_accessory.function: TRAPEZIUS (shrug, head tilt) + STERNOCLEIDOMASTOID (head rotation). tested: shrug against resistance, turn head against resistance.

XII_hypoglossal.function: TONGUE muscles. all intrinsic + most extrinsic tongue muscles. speech, swallowing, food manipulation. damage → tongue deviates TOWARD damaged side when protruded.

spinal_nerves.count: 31 pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal
spinal_nerves.formation: dorsal root (sensory) + ventral root (motor) merge → spinal nerve → immediately splits into dorsal ramus (back) + ventral ramus (front/sides/limbs)
spinal_nerves.dermatomes: area of skin supplied by sensory fibers of ONE spinal nerve. mapped for diagnosing nerve damage level.

plexuses.cervical_C1_C5: neck muscles, diaphragm. PHRENIC NERVE (C3-C5) → diaphragm. 'C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive.'
plexuses.brachial_C5_T1: upper limb. major nerves: musculocutaneous (biceps), median (forearm flexors, thenar), ulnar (hand intrinsics, funny bone), radial (triceps, extensors), axillary (deltoid).
plexuses.lumbar_L1_L4: anterior thigh, medial leg. major nerve: FEMORAL (quads, hip flexion). obturator (adductors).
plexuses.sacral_L4_S3: posterior thigh, leg, foot. major nerve: SCIATIC (largest nerve in body → tibial + common fibular). gluteal nerves.
plexuses.note: no plexus for thoracic (T2-T12) — intercostal nerves go directly between ribs.

overview.what: involuntary motor system. controls smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, glands.
overview.two_neuron_chain: preganglionic neuron (cell body in CNS) → synapse in ganglion → postganglionic neuron (cell body in ganglion) → effector.
overview.dual_innervation: most organs receive BOTH sympathetic + parasympathetic. opposing effects maintain homeostasis.

sympathetic.preganglionic: SHORT. cell body in lateral horn → exits via ventral root → white ramus communicans → sympathetic chain ganglion (or collateral ganglion).
sympathetic.postganglionic: LONG. from ganglion → gray ramus communicans back to spinal nerve → target organ.

ganglia.sympathetic_chain_paravertebral: paired, run alongside vertebral column. most postganglionic neurons here.
ganglia.collateral_prevertebral: unpaired, anterior to vertebral column. celiac ganglion (foregut organs), superior mesenteric (midgut), inferior mesenteric (hindgut).

neurotransmitters.preganglionic: ACh (cholinergic) → nicotinic receptors on postganglionic neuron.
neurotransmitters.postganglionic: NOREPINEPHRINE (NE) (adrenergic) → alpha or beta receptors on target. EXCEPTION: sweat glands → ACh (cholinergic).

sympathetic.adrenal_medulla: modified sympathetic ganglion. preganglionic fibers synapse DIRECTLY on chromaffin cells → release EPINEPHRINE (80%) + NE (20%) into BLOOD. hormonal reinforcement of sympathetic response.

parasympathetic.origin: brainstem (CN III, VII, IX, X) + sacral spinal cord (S2-S4)
parasympathetic.preganglionic: LONG. travels all the way to ganglion NEAR or IN the target organ wall.
parasympathetic.postganglionic: SHORT. very close to or embedded in target organ.
parasympathetic.ganglia: terminal (intramural) ganglia — located NEAR or WITHIN the wall of the target organ.

neurotransmitters.postganglionic: ACh → MUSCARINIC receptors on target. BOTH neurons cholinergic.

parasympathetic.vagus_nerve: CN X carries ~75% of all parasympathetic output. heart, lungs, GI tract through transverse colon.
effects: stimulates urination (relaxes internal urethral sphincter, contracts detrusor)
parasympathetic.does_NOT_innervate: blood vessels (mostly), sweat glands, adrenal medulla, arrector pili. these are sympathetic-only.

cholinergic_ACh.nicotinic: on ALL postganglionic neurons (both sympathetic + parasympathetic) + skeletal muscle NMJ. always EXCITATORY. ion channel (fast).
cholinergic_ACh.muscarinic: on parasympathetic TARGET organs. can be excitatory OR inhibitory depending on organ. G-protein coupled (slower).

adrenergic_NE_Epi.alpha1: smooth muscle CONTRACTION (vasoconstriction of skin + viscera, pupil dilation, urethral sphincter contraction).
adrenergic_NE_Epi.alpha2: presynaptic — inhibits further NE release (negative feedback).
adrenergic_NE_Epi.beta1: HEART. increases rate + force of contraction. 'you have ONE heart' = beta ONE.
adrenergic_NE_Epi.beta2: smooth muscle RELAXATION (bronchodilation, vasodilation in skeletal muscle, uterine relaxation). 'you have TWO lungs' = beta TWO.

autonomic_nervous_system.comparison_table_rule: sympathetic: short pre, long post, NE postganglionic (except sweat = ACh). parasympathetic: long pre, short post, ACh both. opposite in almost every way.

clinical.sciatica: compression/irritation of sciatic nerve. pain radiating down posterior thigh + leg. often from herniated disc at L4-L5 or L5-S1.
clinical.carpal_tunnel: compression of MEDIAN NERVE in carpal tunnel of wrist. numbness/tingling in thumb, index, middle, lateral ring finger. weakness of thenar muscles.
clinical.bells_palsy: CN VII (facial) — unilateral facial paralysis. can't close eye, drooling, can't wrinkle forehead. usually temporary.
clinical.phrenic_nerve_damage: C3-C5. if both phrenic nerves damaged → diaphragm paralyzed → can't breathe independently.
clinical.horners_syndrome: disruption of sympathetic supply to face. ptosis (drooping eyelid), miosis (constricted pupil), anhidrosis (no sweating on affected side).
clinical.atropine: muscarinic antagonist. blocks parasympathetic effects. dilates pupil, increases HR, dries secretions. used pre-surgery.
clinical.beta_blockers: block beta1 receptors. decrease HR + force. treat hypertension, angina, arrhythmia.
